newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan PHS firms to increase investment and bases.
newsitem.headline: Japan PHS firms to increase investment and bases.

text.p: Japan's major operators of the personal handyphone system (PHS) said on Monday that they were increasing their investment and building more base stations nationwide to meet growing demand.

DDI Tokyo Pocket Telephone Inc said it plans to invest 100 billion yen in the current business year ending March 1997 and build about 30,000 more base stations. It now has 28,000 stations, a company spokesman said.
DDI Tokyo Pocket is 85 percent owned by telecommunications carrier DDI Corp.
NTT Personal Communications Network Inc said it plans to add 130,000 base stations to its network across the country, bringing the total number of its stations to 250,000 by the end of March 1997.
This would cost NTT Personal more than 70 billion yen in 1996/97, an NTT Personal spokesman said.
NTT Personal is a member of the Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp (NTT) group.
PHS is a Japan-developed mobile phone system which costs less than a conventional cellphone but has a shorter range and cannot be used inside moving vehicles.

"Some people still think PHS is a cheap cellular phone, but the industry is planning to lauch a new data communications service next spring, which will definitely contribute to its credibility as a multimedia device," the NTT Personal spokesman said.
